neighboring_unit_entries.title: Replace Stirling's phase by theta and expose uniqueness as the RH hinge

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The selected functional-equation phase branch produces labeled critical-line candidates, and equality with the whole-strip count follows if each label has exactly one well-defined solution; this uniqueness premise is the decisive proof obligation.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source ultimately calls the approach non-rigorous and presents uniqueness as argued or assumed, so count matching cannot be detached from that condition.
related_synthesis_entries.title: A phase equation proves RH only if its global uniqueness premise is proved

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The saturation argument has a sharp hinge: if every integer label yields exactly one well-defined solution, the resulting on-line staircase matches the known whole-strip count and leaves no numerical room for other zeros.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source replaces the label by a counting variable using the half-jump convention, obtains an asymptotic N0(T), and observes that it has the same expression as the Riemann-von Mangoldt count N(T).
directed.conceptual_reading: A local uniqueness premise is amplified into a global classification by count saturation; the counting identity is downstream of that premise, not an independent proof of it.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The integer label and the jump of arg ζ form the bridge from individual transcendental equations to a staircase counting function.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion that no additional amplitude-zero or other phase-branch solutions exist is conditional on well-definedness and uniqueness for all labels.
directed.uncertainty: The conditional logic is clear, while the exact half-jump convention, error term, and constants should be checked against the PDF.

supported: The span conditionally converts integer labels into N0(T), obtains the displayed asymptotic staircase, compares it with N(T), and says saturation would leave no additional amplitude-zero or other phase-branch zeros.
inference: Count saturation is a valid conceptual description of how one-solution-per-label would turn an on-line family into a whole-strip classification.
unsupported_or_imported: The source's step from a well-defined displaced argument to monotonicity and a unique solution for every n is asserted rather than proved in this span; calling it a merely 'local uniqueness premise' understates that it is a global all-label existence-and-uniqueness assumption.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: Low otherwise: the analysis distinguishes the conditional hinge from the downstream counting identity instead of restating the formulas.
context_or_ocr_risk: The half-jump convention, constants, error term, and arg-zeta branch require PDF verification, but the conditional logical structure is readable.
missed_mechanism: The comparison with N(T) is used both to assert monotonic behavior and later to claim saturation, so the unproved monotonicity/uniqueness step and potential circularity deserve explicit audit.
revision_instructions: Replace 'local uniqueness premise' with a global existence, well-definedness, monotonicity, and uniqueness assumption for every label; state that the span does not justify this hinge and that count equality follows only after it.
